drug_class: Prostaglandin analog / nitric oxide-donating agent (eye drop)
purpose: This eye drop is used to lower pressure inside your eye. It is prescribed for people with open-angle glaucoma or a condition called ocular hypertension, where eye pressure is too high. Keeping eye pressure under control helps protect your vision and prevent damage to the optic nerve.
how_it_works: When you put this drop in your eye, it breaks down into two active parts that work together. One part helps fluid drain out of your eye more easily, and the other part (nitric oxide) relaxes the tiny blood vessels and tissues in your eye to further reduce pressure. Together, these two actions lower your eye pressure better than either part could do alone.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is a gradual darkening of the iris (the colored part of your eye), which may be permanent. Your eyelashes may also grow longer, thicker, or darker over time. You might notice redness, mild stinging or irritation in the eye, or a feeling like something is in your eye. The skin around your eye may also darken slightly.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have ever had eye surgery, eye infections, or any other eye problems. If you wear contact lenses, remove them before putting in the drop and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in. Do not use more drops than prescribed — using too much will not lower your pressure faster and could cause problems. Tell your doctor about all other eye drops or medications you are taking. If you experience sudden vision changes, severe eye pain, or signs of an eye infection, contact your doctor right away.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one drop in the affected eye (or both eyes) once a day, in the evening. Try to use it at the same time each night. Wash your hands before using the drops, tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid gently, and place one drop inside. Press lightly on the inner corner of your eye for about one to two minutes after the drop to help keep it in your eye.
